reason: Weathered rock can contain coloured minerals, making it a plausible source of pigment for painting.
expectation: Water and coloured minerals may make a usable paint.

effect: The rock and water made pigment, so it can now be used for painting in the cave.
reaction: The coloured mineral grains make a satisfying practical link to painting.
reason: The pigment can leave marks on the cave wall, so the cave is the natural place to use it.
expectation: The pigment will be used to paint on the cave wall, possibly advancing the imaginary-animal goal.

effect: The pigment and memory produced a painting of a remembered animal, but the imaginary-animal goal remains open.
reaction: The distinction between depicting an absent animal and inventing one is interesting.
reason: A story may help turn the existing animal image into an imagined creature.
expectation: The story may inspire a painting of an animal that does not exist.

effect: The story transformed the painting into an imagined beast, completing that goal and revealing a night-sky painting goal.
reaction: Combining familiar features into an invented creature is a clear illustration of imagination.
reason: Stars are the natural subject for the newly revealed night-sky goal, and the cave is the painting surface.
expectation: The stars may inspire a painted night sky in the cave.

effect: Stars and pigment made the imagined painted sky, completing that goal; singing together remains.
reaction: Choosing an arrangement rather than copying the sky makes the imagined aspect clear.
reason: A call shared by the social group seems a plausible starting point for singing together.
expectation: The group may use their calls to sing together.
